'''Curtis Tracy McMullen''' (born May 21, 1958) is an American mathematician who is the Cabot Professor of Mathematics at [[Harvard University]].  He was awarded the [[Fields Medal]] in 1998 for his work in [[complex dynamics]], [[hyperbolic geometry]] and [[Teichmüller theory]].

==Biography==

McMullen graduated as [[valedictorian]] in 1980 from [[Williams College]] and obtained his [[PhD]] in 1985 from  [[Harvard University]], supervised by [[Dennis Sullivan]].  He held post-doctoral positions at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]], and the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], after which he was on the faculty at [[Princeton University]] (1987–1990) and the [[University of California, Berkeley]] (1990–1997), before joining Harvard in 1997.
McMullen was chair of the [[Harvard Mathematics Department]] from 2017 to 2020. His doctoral student [[Maryam Mirzakhani]] was the first woman to win the [[Fields Medal]].

==Honors and awards==
McMullen received the [[Salem Prize]] in 1991 and won the [[Fields Medal]] in 1998<ref>[https://www.ams.org/notices/199810/comm-fields.pdf Borcherds, Gowers, Kontsevich, and McMullen Receive Fields Medals]</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Lepowsky, James|author2=Lindenstrauss, Joram|author3=Manin, Yuri I.|author4=Milnor, John|title=The Mathematical Work of the 1998 Fields Medalists|journal=Notices of the AMS|date=January 1999|volume=46|issue=1|pages=17–26|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/199901/fields.pdf}}</ref> at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] (ICM) in Berlin.<ref>{{cite book|author=McMullen, Curtis T.|chapter=Rigidity and inflexibility in conformal dynamics|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. II|year=1998|pages=841–855|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011671000}}</ref> At the 1990 ICM in Kyoto he was an Invited Speaker.<ref>{{cite book|author=McMullen, Curtis T.|year=1991|chapter=Rational maps and Kleinian groups|title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, August 21-29, 1990, Kyoto, Japan|editor=Satake, Ichiro|pages=889–900|location=Tokyo|publisher=Springer}}</ref> He was awarded a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] in 2004, elected to the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] in 2007, and received the [[Humboldt Research Award]] in 2011.
